messages:
andy_support: FYI customer relay — during a scheduled pentest they saw intermittent 401s and then reported they could enumerate a KMS alias. attaching initial notes. :eyes:

and y_support: Steps they ran (from pen tester):
```bash
# quick check they said worked:
aws kms list-aliases --region us-west-2 --profile test-pen
# then try a call that should be audited:
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --LookupAttributes AttributeKey=EventId,AttributeValue=<some-event-id>
```

mike_redteam: confirm — I ran a limited repro in a staging account. ListAliases returned metadata while CloudTrail had no corresponding KMS ListAliases event for ~30s window. I have one request-id: r-0a1b2c3d4e5f.

sarah_sec: can you paste the exact CloudTrail query & event id (redacted) so we can compare with API gateway logs? also pinging @jamie_ops for infra traces.

mike_redteam: pasted (redacted):
```json
{"eventTime":"2026-02-26T18:12:03Z","eventName":"ListAliases","requestParameters":{},"requestID":"r-0a1b2c3d4e5f"}
```

jamie_ops: looking at ingress logs for that time in us-west-2. Gateway has a 200 for the ListAliases at 18:12:03, but our KMS proxy shows a 404 to the internal audit forwarder around the same time. suspect intermittent forwarder backlog. investigating queue metrics now.

nina_privacy: note: customer asked if this implies data-retention gap for audit logs. we need to be precise in communications. If CloudTrail misses events, compliance impact could be medium-high depending on retention window.

andy_support: customer is on enterprise dedicated. they want severity elevated until we confirm no lost audit records. also raised billing anomaly: tokens incremented during these api probes but no corresponding model calls. possible unauthorized request pattern.

jamie_ops: found increased write-latency spikes on our audit-forwarder service at 18:11-18:13 UTC. backlog spiked to 4k items for ~45s then drained. there was a GC pause on one of the forwarder pods (g1) and a transient DB failover for the metadata store. forwarding failed => CloudTrail ingestion downstream missed some entries.

sarah_sec: thanks. what's the mitigation? can we recover missing events?

jamie_ops: immediate mitigations: (1) bring extra replicas up (done), (2) throttle incoming ListAliases from external IPs for the pen window, (3) enable synchronous write fallback for audit-forwarder for 24h while we repair DB replication.

mike_redteam: can you confirm we'll re-run pen tests only after we provide reproduction steps so I can validate? happy to wait but want retest window.

andy_support: agreed. customer requested timeline and wants evidence when fixed. they also asked for itemized root cause and whether KMS keys were exposed.

sarah_sec: early verdict — KMS keys not exposed. ListAliases reveals metadata but no key material returned. severity contested: pen team says enumeration lowers confidentiality profile; customers worry about compliance posture. we need a short findings statement for legal & customer.

nina_privacy: suggested line: "During a transient audit ingestion failure, audit events for certain KMS control-plane calls were delayed and a small window of event ingestion was not recorded in the downstream audit index. We have identified the cause (audit-forwarder backlog + DB failover) and implemented mitigations. No key material was exposed and we are performing a thorough retention reconciliation."

sarah_sec: +1 to nina's wording. also list remediation items and timeline.

jamie_ops: Actions (short):
- Patch forwarder to use connection pool guard (in review)
- Force-replay CloudTrail source logs to downstream index for 18:10-18:20 UTC (in progress)
- Add alert: audit-forwarder queue > 500 triggers auto-scale (PR opened)
- Add e2e test to simulate DB failover under load (task filed)

andy_support: for the replay: can you confirm scope (customer vs global) — customer wants assurance their tenant logs are intact.

jamie_ops: replay is per-region; we will reconstruct the index slice for the customer by filtering by account-id and time window. estimate 3h to complete replay and provide a digest.

mike_redteam: will schedule retest 24h after you confirm replay finished. I'll run ListAliases + CloudTrail lookup and attach the two outputs for comparison.

sarah_sec: decision: severity set to P2 for now (customer-facing, potential compliance impact). we'll send an interim statement to the customer in 4 hours. @andy_support to own comms.

andy_support: prepping message now. draft: "We identified a transient ingestion issue that impacted audit visibility for a short window. We are replaying event sources and will provide a reconciliation report within 3 hours. No evidence of key material exposure." will share draft in #incidents.

deploy-bot: deploy started: forwarder-fix-v1 -> canary (jenkins #5499) :rocket: 

jamie_ops: canary metrics look healthy, queue drained. replay job started, scanning cloudtrail logs for r-0a1b2c3d4e5f.

mike_redteam: once replay completes I'll compare outputs. leaving a note: when you replay, include original requestID fields; pen toolkit matches on requestID+eventTime.

nina_privacy: also ensure retention proof: we need a signed manifest showing ingestion timestamps for the customer's account for the window. legal asked for cryptographic timestamping if possible.

jamie_ops: adding signed manifest step to replay job. will store manifest in customer audit bucket with restricted ACL and place SHA256 hash in the incident ticket.

andy_support: customer update queued. will send interim note with apologies, planned replay, and ETA 3h.

sarah_sec: after replay and retest, we will close or downgrade severity. action items assigned to: jamie_ops (replay + manifest), nina_privacy (wording + compliance impact), andy_support (customer comms), mike_redteam (retest + evidence).

mike_redteam: ack. will stand by. :lock:

andy_support: thanks team — I'll post the final reconciliation artifacts here when jamie signals replay done.
